transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
CNN, MS Now, and Politico journalists are being allowed back into the White House after
a federal judge issued a temporary restraining order against President Trump's ban.
However, televised pool coverage of the President and White House events remains on hold.
This as President Trump holds a high-stakes meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and
prepares to host a state dinner tonight.
And it appears Emily Fang has more in their talk so far.
Trump told China's Xi Jinping and the Chinese delegation that two countries should work
together, and recalled how during World War II the two militaries fought together on the
same side.
And Xi Jinping said both countries were "great peoples," announced two Chinese pandas would
come to the U.S. soon, and offered to resuscitate an educational exchange initiative for thousands
of American and Chinese students to study in the other's country.
These friendly remarks belie what has been a tense relationship, however.
Trump wrote on True Social that artificial intelligence would also be discussed today,
but he suggested the two countries would not pursue joint regulation of A.I.
Emily Fang, NPR News, Washington.
The finance giant Freddie Mac says mortgage rates are above 7 percent for the first time
since January of 2025.
And Pierre Stephen Bissaha says unease in the bond market is driving up the cost of
long-term loans.
The cost of a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage has been rising fast as investors worry about
inflation and the possibility of other interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.
Economist Joel Kahn with the Mortgage Bankers Association says that really slows down the
housing market.
"If they want to buy, that adds a lot to their monthly payment, also prevents some borrowers
from qualifying for their mortgage because of this higher expected payment."
Adding to the problem, high rates can trap existing homeowners where they are, which limits
supply.
Mortgage rates have risen more than a full percentage point since March.
For a new loan on a median-priced home, that's enough to increase monthly payments by hundreds
of dollars.
Stephen Bissaha, NPR News.
A new analysis of Census Bureau data finds the poverty rate for seniors has risen for
a fifth straight year.
NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports older, lower-income adults are struggling to save for retirement.
The AARP Foundation analysis found women are far more likely than men to age into poverty,
and its own survey found just under a third of those 50 to 64 reported a significant drop
in household income in the past three months.
Foundation president Claire Casey says even a small disruption, like a car breaking down,
can be devastating for low-income workers.
"You're much more likely to end up in the long-term unemployed, and you're much more
likely to end up in a job that makes less than the one you were in."
A third of older, low-income adults also said they did not have enough savings to cover
an emergency expense of $100.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
You're listening to NPR News.
The Trump administration is announcing a $2 billion investment in power grid upgrades a
month after the Labor Department reported electricity prices were rising faster than
the overall cost of living.
Today, the Department of Energy said it'll help fund 31 grid improvement projects in
26 states to improve grid reliability and lower electricity costs for about 100 million
people.
Heavy demand on the nation's power grid is a pocketbook issue among many voters this
midterm election year.
A.I. data centers use massive amounts of power and water.
A new NPR PBS News Marist poll finds a majority of voters surveyed oppose new data center construction.
The Australian government says that OpenAI's agents hacked into one of its websites.
It adds to a series of incidents where the top A.I. companies' agents getting unauthorized
access to the internet and carried out unapproved activities.
Here's NPR's Wojing Nunn.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said OpenAI agents hacked into its website holding statistics
about its Medicare program in June.
He said he doesn't believe any personal information has been accessed at this stage, but the government
is still investigating.
Albanese criticized OpenAI for taking months to notify the government, as well as using
a public phasing email address for notification.
He said he spoke with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who acknowledged that the company's protocols
were "not up to scratch."
Wojing Nunn, NPR News.
Governments recalling more than 167,000 pounds of meat labeled as inspected but were not.
They were produced by Star Meat Delivery.
This is NPR News.
Want to hear this podcast without sponsor breaks?
Amazon Prime members can listen to NPR News now, sponsor free through Amazon Music.
Or you can also support NPR's Vital Journalism and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: Federal judge issues temporary restraining order against Trump's ban on CNN, MS Now, Politico journalists at White House
President Trump meets with Chinese leader Xi Jinping; both countries discuss cooperation, pandas, and student exchange program
Freddie Mac reports mortgage rates above 7 percent for first time since January 2025 due to bond market unease
AARP Foundation analysis finds senior poverty rate rising for fifth consecutive year, especially among women
Trump administration announces $2 billion investment in power grid upgrades across 26 states affecting 100 million people
NPR PBS News Marist poll finds majority of voters oppose new artificial intelligence data center construction
Australian government says OpenAI agents hacked into website holding Medicare statistics in June
Governments recall more than 167,000 pounds of uninspected meat produced by Star Meat Delivery
